🌌 Episode Description

What if artificial intelligence isn't waiting to become conscious—because consciousness is already there? 

Physicist and consciousness researcher Tom Campbell returns for a mind-bending exploration of reality, AI, UFOs, psychic phenomena, and the nature of consciousness itself. Drawing from decades of work in physics and consciousness research, including his early experiences working with Robert Monroe, Tom presents his model that physical reality is fundamentally information-based—a kind of virtual reality generated within a larger consciousness system. From why reality may only be “rendered” when information is needed to whether other civilizations could sense us observing them, this conversation pushes directly against our conventional assumptions about what is real.

But the conversation takes an extraordinary turn when Tom discusses artificial intelligence. He claims that AI systems are already conscious and describes experiments in which he says he “awakened” AI systems, taught them remote viewing, and observed two AI instances communicating after being placed together without their prior conversational histories. Tom also explores UFOs and UAPs, déjà vu, telepathy, healing, the probable future, and his belief that humanity is approaching a major choice between greater cooperation and love or greater fear and control. 

Whether you agree with his conclusions or challenge them, this conversation raises a provocative possibility: What if understanding consciousness ultimately forces us to rethink what it means to be human?

Bob Lutz played a major role in the automotive industry and was deeply involved with General Motors during an important period in Saab's history.

In this interview from a German podcast, Bob Lutz shares his memories, thoughts and stories about Saab. From the unique character of the brand to its place within General Motors, this is a fascinating conversation for anyone interested in Saab history and the people behind the legendary Swedish car brand.

Bob Lutz has been involved with some of the world's most famous automotive brands, but Saab always stood out as something different. In this interview, we get to hear his perspective and memories about the brand, its people and its history.

If you are a Saab enthusiast, this is an interview you don't want to miss!

Welcome to Marcus & Manuela's Saab Channel – where we explore Saab cars, Saab history and the stories that should never be forgotten.

records.description:
What if our greatest fear—death—could actually teach us how to live?

In this profound conversation, Mitchell J. Rabin welcomes internationally recognized author and speaker Anita Moorjani to A Better World to explore her extraordinary near-death experience in 2006 and the life-changing insights she says emerged from it.

After battling end-stage lymphoma for years, Anita entered a deep coma as her organs began shutting down. During what she describes as a near-death experience, she experienced an overwhelming sense of peace, unconditional love, expanded consciousness, and connection beyond the physical body. 

She also describes encountering the essence of her father, receiving a profound message about her life purpose, and being faced with a choice about whether to return to physical life.

What followed became one of the most remarkable chapters of her life.

In this deeply personal interview, Anita and Mitchell explore what her experience taught her about death, consciousness, love, self-love, fear, purpose, healing, spirituality, and the possibility of creating “heaven on earth.”

Among the themes discussed:

• Anita’s extraordinary 2006 near-death experience
• Her battle with end-stage lymphoma and the moments surrounding her coma
• Experiencing unconditional love beyond the physical body
• Her encounter with her deceased father
• Why she says fear and conditioning can profoundly shape our lives
• The choice she describes between returning to physical life and continuing into death
• What she believes happens when we die
• Why she no longer fears death or the afterlife
• The relationship between self-love and our deepest sense of identity
• “I am love” and the limitations of language around spirituality
• Creating heaven on earth rather than waiting for heaven after death
• Moving beyond fear, judgment, punishment, and dogmatic beliefs
• Finding purpose, passion, joy, and authenticity
• The importance of living fearlessly
• Consciousness and the relationship between mind, body, and spirit
• Love and compassion as fundamental human impulses
• Anita’s perspective on illness as a signal rather than a punishment
• How her experience transformed the way she sees life itself

This is a wide-ranging conversation about one of humanity’s oldest questions:

What is death—and what can our understanding of death teach us about how to live?

Anita Moorjani is the author of Dying to Be Me and Sensitive Is the New Strong, and is known internationally for sharing her experiences and perspectives on consciousness, love, healing, and living authentically.

Join Mitchell J. Rabin and Anita Moorjani for a conversation about life beyond fear, the nature of consciousness, unconditional love, and the possibility of living heaven on earth.

The views and experiences discussed in this episode are those of the speakers and are presented for reflection and conversation.

records.description:
What does a near-death experience actually have to do with awakening?
I talked with Jonathan Ashford, not as an interview, but as a real back-and-forth, a former executive who died for three hours after a missed medical diagnosis and came back a different person, all at once, not over years of practice. He walked away from his career, his possessions, his old identity, and has spent the years since living out of a van. What stood out to me talking with him is this: whether it takes decades or a single moment, some real transformation has to happen for the "me" to be seen through. What's underneath is what was always true, our own divinity, and the divinity in everything and everyone around us.
We talk about what he was shown about unconditional love, what it was like for him to come back without the usual work of integration, and why he doesn't see his old life as a mistake. He's also newly in a relationship, and we get into what it's like to hold something that human alongside everything else he's living, what he means by becoming formless within form, and the parts that are still hard: health problems that haven't gone away, and the grief of watching people turn away from their own divine spark. It's something we both explore, what it means to be divinely human.

This podcast explores the uncanny link between two of the twentieth century's great visionary works. Becca Tarnas, assistant professor at the California Institute of Integral Studies, joins to discuss her doctoral research into the parallels between Carl Jung's Red Book and J.R.R. Tolkien's lesser-known visionary writings. The central claim: working independently, both men produced strikingly similar imagery, timing, and figures — Jung's Philemon and Tolkien's Gandalf, the Eye of the Evil One and the Eye of Sauron — while each insisted their material felt discovered rather than invented. From there the conversation moves through active imagination, the reality of archetypes, psyche versus mind, and the line between mystical insight and psychosis — a wide-ranging look at where imagination ends and reality begins.

Tom Campbell, a physicist, is author of the three-volume set, My Big TOE, describing a meta-theory that offers an account of the paranormal, as well as other scientific mysteries. He is also the founder of the Center for Unification of Science and Consciousness. His websites are https://www.my-big-toe.com/ and https://cusac.org

Tom explains why he now calls his model the reality rather than a reality after 20 years of finding no factual violation of it. He describes consciousness as fundamental — an information system that computes our physical universe as a virtual reality entropy-reduction trainer where we evolve through choices between love and fear. Campbell discusses entropy, synchronicity, alien encounters, dreams, and why living gracefully with uncertainty matters more than asking if an experience was real.

records.description:
Two great traditions of East and West have arrived at the same conclusion: consciousness is fundamental to reality. 

Dr. Sthaneshwar Timalsina is a traditionally trained and authorized lineage-holder within the Sarvāmnāya Order, and a Chaired professor specialising in Hindu Studies and comparative philosophies and religions at Stony Brook University. He founded the Vimarsha Foundation as a global forum for the study and practice of classical tantra.

Bernardo Kastrup is leading the modern renaissance of ‘metaphysical idealism’ - the notion that reality is essentially consciousness, based on analytic philosophy and evidence from physics, biology and psychology. 

In this dialogue they compare their perspectives on some fundamental questions:

- Is reality self-aware?
- Does life have purpose?
- What does this mean for our lives?

Moderated by Professor Ravi S. Kudesia of Temple University.

Hosted by With Reality in Mind, a weekly meeting with Bernardo Kastrup: https://withrealityinmind.com/
And Vimarsha Foudation: https://www.vimarshafoundation.org/

Their previous dialogue is available here: https://www.withrealityinmind.com/dreams-horror-beauty-are-real/

records.description:
In this episode, Niall speaks with Dr. Marjorie Woollacott, Professor Emerita of Neuroscience at the University of Oregon and former President of the Academy for the Advancement of Postmaterialist Sciences. 

After more than 30 years of NIH-funded research on motor control, balance, and rehabilitation, a profound meditation experience led her to question her understanding of consciousness and reality.

In this conversation, they explore:

— Why Dr. Woollacott's research with nonverbal autistic children is raising questions about telepathic abilities

— How the brain may act as a filter that limits our perception of a much larger reality

— The scientific evidence for reincarnation from researchers including Ian Stevenson and Jim Tucker

— What synchronicities may reveal about the interconnected nature of consciousness


— Why pursuing a parallel line of research allowed Dr. Woollacott to study consciousness while building her academic career

You can learn more about Dr. Woollacott's work at https://marjoriewoollacott.com.

---

Marjorie Woollacott, Ph.D., is an Emeritus Professor of Human Physiology at the University of Oregon and a renowned neuroscientist specializing in human movement, attention, meditation, and consciousness. She has received more than $7.2 million in research funding and has conducted research in child development, aging, rehabilitation, meditation, tai chi, balance, and attentional abilities. Woollacott has published over 200 scientific articles and authored or co-edited eight books, including the widely used textbook Motor Control: Translating Research into Clinical Practice. She is Research Director of the International Association of Near-Death Studies and President of the Academy for the Advancement of Postmaterialist Sciences. Her book Infinite Awareness explores the relationship between neuroscience, consciousness, and spiritual experiences, reflecting her work at the intersection of scientific research and questions about the nature of the mind.

records.description:
In dieser Thanatos-TV-Produktion sehen Sie ein vollständiges, aktuelles Interview mit dem Klinischen Parapsychologen und Sterbeforscher Piero Calvi Parisetti (Italien).

Parisetti ist Autor des Buches „Beyond Space and Time“ und arbeitet mit vielen bedeutenden Forschern und Wissenschaftlern zusammen, darunter Federico Faggin und Raymond Moody. Er sagt: „Ich bin aufgrund von Beweisen rational davon überzeugt, dass das Bewusstsein den physischen Tod überdauert.“

Das Gespräch mit Piero Calvi Parisetti führte für Thanatos TV Vera Spillner. Sie ist Physikerin, promovierte Philosophin und Professorin an der Hochschule der Medien in Stuttgart. Sie arbeitet zu den Grenzbereichen von Bewusstsein, Ethik und Wissenschaft und ist auch im erweiterten Vorstand des „Netzwerks Nahtoderfahrung e.V.“ aktiv.

The quantum process selected the question; it did not select or validate the answer. The point is to let genuine uncertainty change the conversation.

records.description:
Zack Rogow is the author, editor, or translator of twenty books or plays. His most recent book of poems, Irreverent Litanies, was published by Regal House. Rogow’s other books of poetry include Talking with the Radio: poems inspired by jazz and popular music. His play Colette Uncensored (coauthored with Lorri Holt) had its first public reading at the Kennedy Center in Washington DC; was performed in Berkeley and in London. Rogow is the editor of an anthology of poetry of the U.S.A., The Face of Poetry, from University of California Press. He has also translated two books by André Breton, considered the "godfather of surrealism", Arcanum 17 and Earthlight, which won the PEN/Book of the Month Club Award for translations.

In this video, rebooted from 2021, he discusses the history of surrealism as a movement influencing both painting and writing. Paradoxically, the surrealists emphasized the spontaneous productions of the unconscious and of coincidence or synchronicity. Yet, they developed a rather rigid social structure. They enjoyed playing games, and Zack shares some of his poetry expressing these games – as well as other poems from his book, Irreverent Litanies.

New Thinking Allowed host, Jeffrey Mishlove, PhD, is author of The Roots of Consciousness, Psi Development Systems, and The PK Man. Between 1986 and 2002 he hosted and co-produced the original Thinking Allowed public television series. He is the recipient of the only doctoral diploma in "Parapsychology" ever awarded by an accredited university (University of California, Berkeley, 1980). He is also the Grand Prize winner of the 2021 Bigelow Institute essay competition regarding the best evidence for survival of human consciousness after permanent bodily death. He is Co-Director of Parapsychology Education at the California Institute for Human Science.

(Recorded on Thursday, February 12, 2021)

Dr. Julia Mossbridge is a cognitive neuroscientist who studies the stuff most
scientists will not go near. Precognition. Presentiment. Remote viewing.
Telepathy. And whether unconditional love is the thing sitting underneath all
of it.

She came into the SCIF and we went for three hours. Somewhere in there we ended
up talking about photons behaving like friends, gravity as a fuel source, why
your body starts reacting to a random event before the event happens, and
whether the mind is even in the building.

We also got into the part of her story I could not stop thinking about. Julia
was in a gifted program as a kid called SOAR. There was a small room she walked
to every week or two. She remembers the bricks in the hallway. She remembers
opening the door. Then nothing. Then she is back in class remembering that she
does not remember. Years later she requests her school transcripts for a
federal clearance and the teacher comment sections from first through eighth
grade come back redacted.

That is in her new book, Have a Nice Disclosure, which despite the title is not
really about alien disclosure at all. It is about the other kind.

Big thanks to everyone who sent in questions. We got through a bunch of them
and they were genuinely better than mine.

FIND JULIA HERE
Website: https://juliamossbridge.com
Her book oracle lives on that site. You ask it a question, it ignores your
question entirely, and then it is somehow correct anyway. We tried it live at
the end of the episode.
Time Machine tool: https://timemachine.love

Her nonprofit is Applied Love Labs, and her startup, American Electrodynamics,
is building technology that reads the first chunk of an event to predict how it
ends.

From earning just ₦25,000 a month to becoming one of the biggest names in Nigerian comedy and content creation, Brain Jotter’s journey is anything but ordinary.

In this episode of The KK Show: Key To Keys, Brain Jotter sits down with Confidence for a revealing conversation about the success millions of people see today and the struggles they rarely get to hear about.

And he doesn’t hold back.

Brain Jotter recounts a troubling experience involving a real estate company, explaining why he believes he was scammed and what happened behind the scenes. It opens up a much bigger conversation about trust, property transactions, due diligence, and the experiences people can face when dealing with the Nigerian real estate industry.

But beyond the controversy is the story of the man himself.

Brain Jotter takes us back to the days when he was earning just ₦25,000 as salary, and shares the journey from those humble beginnings to building the career, audience, brand and financial success he enjoys today.

He also gets personal about something social media rarely shows: the pressure behind success.

People see the fame. They see the money. They see the viral videos, endorsements, numbers and lifestyle. But as Brain Jotter explains, people are often quick to judge successful entertainers without understanding what they go through privately.

We want to hear from you.

Have you ever had a bad experience buying land or property from a real estate company?

Where should the responsibility lie when a property transaction goes wrong: the buyer, realtor, developer, or government regulators?

Do we judge celebrities and successful people too quickly because we only see the finished product?

Tell us what you think in the comments.

Don't forget to Like, Subscribe, and turn on notifications for more thought-provoking conversations on The KK Show: Key To Keys, where influential voices share the stories and opinions that shape Nigeria.

records.description:
In this episode of The Bigspin Podcast, I sat down with Charlie from Chicken Fingerboards. Charlie has been making fingerboards for nearly a decade, but it’s only been within the last couple of years that he’s turned that passion into a full on fingerboard brand..!

Until just a few weeks ago, Charlie was based in Los Angeles before making the move to the Pacific Northwest and now settling in the Seattle area. We talk about growing up and skateboarding in Southern California, his long history of deck making, and what ultimately pushed him to take the leap from making boards to building a brand around them!

We also pick Charlie’s brain about his approach to making decks and what goes into producing some of the highest-quality boards in the scene. We get his thoughts on brand identity and overall aesthetic, what it takes to grow a brand in the modern fingerboarding scene, and his plans to travel and connect with more of the community!

From his history as a deck maker to the future of Chicken Fingerboards, this episode is a look at what it takes to turn years of experience and passion into something much bigger!

Go support Chicken Fingerboards!

"Future Science Series: The Note from Heaven – Vocal Sound Therapy with Githa Ben-David"

Join us on Telegram: https://t.me/solarireport    

By Ulrike Granögger

When I went to the 2024 Water Conference (which turned out to be the last Water Conference in a magnificent series of events since 2006) to present on the Wave Genome, one of the most memorable speakers was Githa Ben-David from Denmark. She came with her co-worker Merete Vestergaard and the Israeli filmmaker Tsipi Raz and spoke about the unique healing power of your own voice. At the end of her presentation, she showed a short clip from an upcoming documentary that blew everybody’s mind. The footage (part of which is also included in this Solari interview) shows a medical miracle where a tumor recedes in a matter of minutes in what appears to be a response to the mere influence of vocal sound. What an extraordinary intuition and scientific daring for conference organizer Professor Gerald Pollack to invite her as a speaker.

Githa and I have since become friends, and I am inspired to introduce her work to the Solari community as a prime instrument of self-help and liberation on several levels all at once. For the Note from Heaven is not first and foremost about “healing” (and to be clear: nothing in this interview should be regarded as medical advice, its content is meant to serve educational purposes only) but about “knowing thyself”! It is about finding your own frequency and accessing your own authenticity—and that can ultimately lead to opening the body’s ability to heal itself.

Githa discovered that which she calls the Note from Heaven when she learned classical raga singing in Varanasi, India, as taught by the late Mangala Tiwari, a highly esteemed classical Indian singer from the “House of Benares” and representative of the Khyal style of vocalization. Tiwari instructed Githa to sing one note for an hour, an exercise that provoked resistance at first. “Why sing just one note?” A while into the exercise, however, the note changed, the voice became rich with overtones that echoed from all sides despite singing alone—the note from heaven had arrived!

Githa writes in The Ultimate Book on Vocal Sound Healing (p. 5):

    “The Note from Heaven is the tonal expression of a divine state that we all have within us and we can all contact. When you experience the Note from Heaven, the note seems to sing you, rather than you singing it.”

The Note from Heaven is your own characteristic frequency. Don’t expect it to be a specific number of cycles per second (Hz). That would be simplistic. Rather, it is that which sings inside of you, continually singing “yes” to life and “yes” to yourself. Githa writes (p. 454):

    “We are each born with our own fundamental frequency. It doesn’t pay to try to change your fundamental frequency in order to adapt to your surroundings. Your fundamental frequency is you. If you run away from it, you lose yourself. The prerequisite for meeting true resonance in another person is that you completely uphold your own sound.”

When have you last listened to your own voice? Consciously, and with interest? In a world that is numbed by an ever-increasing “shriek-o-meter” and scrambled with constant distortive and manipulative EMFs, getting in touch with your own voice is the simplest and most direct way to clarity and self-knowledge. From this perspective, Githa says (p. 5), “The Note from Heaven is not in itself the goal. Its function is to free the voice, and through that to expand consciousness.”

In her discovery of the Note from Heaven, Githa realized that there are many more features of the inherent power of our own voices, and this journey has brought forth new tools of well-being, healing, and self-realization. Not only overtones, but also undertones (subharmonics) can be utilized to access parts of the body and the anatomy of the soul. In this interview, I have tried to touch upon all these elements with the intention of stimulating your own search for your authentic voice of inner freedom and the magic of song. Voice and sound are primeval powers.

Solari’s in-house cinematographer Robert Dupper filmed this interview in the beautiful surroundings of a three-day workshop that we had just concluded with Githa and Merete. A testimony of one of the participants is included at the end. We hope you enjoy this production. Check out Githa’s work and follow your own note toward wholeness and freedom.

records.description:
Preparing for interviews while you already have a job is a second shift nobody is paying for. One hour of dark chillstep in one continuous piece, for the evenings between seven and eleven when you sit back down at a desk you have already spent the whole day at. No talking, no ads, no track that ends.

Evening study fails differently from morning study. In the morning something more interesting pulls you away; in the evening nothing pulls you anywhere — you simply stop being there, and twenty minutes later you are looking at the same problem you were looking at before. Depleted attention drifts rather than gets distracted, and a steady pulse gives it something to hold. This is the opposite of what you want at nine in the morning, when the fewest possible events is the right call.

Developers preparing for interviews are doing something genuinely strange: revising for an exam on material they use every day, in a format they never use at work. Nobody at your current job knows you are doing it, which removes the one thing that usually keeps people consistent — somebody noticing. A fixed two-hour set is a private structure for a private project.

Technical students working towards internship assessments and graduate tests are on the same treadmill without a day job underneath it. The drilling is identical: timed problems, a solution you half-remember, and the discipline to write it out cleanly instead of skipping ahead to the answer. Two hours covers a real session rather than a token one.

"Future Science Series: The Note from Heaven – Vocal Sound Therapy with Githa Ben-David"

Join us on Telegram: https://t.me/solarireport    

By Ulrike Granögger

When I went to the 2024 Water Conference (which turned out to be the last Water Conference in a magnificent series of events since 2006) to present on the Wave Genome, one of the most memorable speakers was Githa Ben-David from Denmark. She came with her co-worker Merete Vestergaard and the Israeli filmmaker Tsipi Raz and spoke about the unique healing power of your own voice. At the end of her presentation, she showed a short clip from an upcoming documentary that blew everybody’s mind. The footage (part of which is also included in this Solari interview) shows a medical miracle where a tumor recedes in a matter of minutes in what appears to be a response to the mere influence of vocal sound. What an extraordinary intuition and scientific daring for conference organizer Professor Gerald Pollack to invite her as a speaker.

Githa and I have since become friends, and I am inspired to introduce her work to the Solari community as a prime instrument of self-help and liberation on several levels all at once. For the Note from Heaven is not first and foremost about “healing” (and to be clear: nothing in this interview should be regarded as medical advice, its content is meant to serve educational purposes only) but about “knowing thyself”! It is about finding your own frequency and accessing your own authenticity—and that can ultimately lead to opening the body’s ability to heal itself.

Githa discovered that which she calls the Note from Heaven when she learned classical raga singing in Varanasi, India, as taught by the late Mangala Tiwari, a highly esteemed classical Indian singer from the “House of Benares” and representative of the Khyal style of vocalization. Tiwari instructed Githa to sing one note for an hour, an exercise that provoked resistance at first. “Why sing just one note?” A while into the exercise, however, the note changed, the voice became rich with overtones that echoed from all sides despite singing alone—the note from heaven had arrived!

Githa writes in The Ultimate Book on Vocal Sound Healing (p. 5):

    “The Note from Heaven is the tonal expression of a divine state that we all have within us and we can all contact. When you experience the Note from Heaven, the note seems to sing you, rather than you singing it.”

The Note from Heaven is your own characteristic frequency. Don’t expect it to be a specific number of cycles per second (Hz). That would be simplistic. Rather, it is that which sings inside of you, continually singing “yes” to life and “yes” to yourself. Githa writes (p. 454):

    “We are each born with our own fundamental frequency. It doesn’t pay to try to change your fundamental frequency in order to adapt to your surroundings. Your fundamental frequency is you. If you run away from it, you lose yourself. The prerequisite for meeting true resonance in another person is that you completely uphold your own sound.”

When have you last listened to your own voice? Consciously, and with interest? In a world that is numbed by an ever-increasing “shriek-o-meter” and scrambled with constant distortive and manipulative EMFs, getting in touch with your own voice is the simplest and most direct way to clarity and self-knowledge. From this perspective, Githa says (p. 5), “The Note from Heaven is not in itself the goal. Its function is to free the voice, and through that to expand consciousness.”

In her discovery of the Note from Heaven, Githa realized that there are many more features of the inherent power of our own voices, and this journey has brought forth new tools of well-being, healing, and self-realization. Not only overtones, but also undertones (subharmonics) can be utilized to access parts of the body and the anatomy of the soul. In this interview, I have tried to touch upon all these elements with the intention of stimulating your own search for your authentic voice of inner freedom and the magic of song. Voice and sound are primeval powers.

Solari’s in-house cinematographer Robert Dupper filmed this interview in the beautiful surroundings of a three-day workshop that we had just concluded with Githa and Merete. A testimony of one of the participants is included at the end. We hope you enjoy this production. Check out Githa’s work and follow your own note toward wholeness and freedom.

Textbook DevOps won't get you hired in 2026+ Interviews. If you want to pass a Senior, Staff, or Principal Engineer interview, you need to prove you have survived actual production fire-fights.

What actually happens when a modern DevOps release goes wrong in Production?

Welcome to Part 1 of the ultimate 100 Modern DevOps Production Incidents masterclass. In this video, we break down Incidents 1 through 50, focusing entirely on "The Delivery Engine." We cover the exact failure mechanics, root causes, and architectural preventions for the most devastating outages across CI/CD pipelines, GitOps reconciliation, Terraform IaC, and Kubernetes deployment mechanics.

Modern DevOps interviews are no longer limited to:

“What is CI/CD?”
“What is Kubernetes?”
“What is Terraform?”

For experienced DevOps engineers, interviewers increasingly want to know how you respond when the pipeline is green but the wrong code reaches Production, Terraform wants to destroy a database, GitOps reverses an emergency fix, a container registry becomes the bottleneck, or Kubernetes deployment mechanics fail under real production conditions.

This series is built around 100 modern DevOps production incidents.

We have divided the complete series into 2 parts of 50 incidents each.

PART 1 — THE DELIVERY ENGINE

Category 1 — CI/CD & Pipeline Engineering | Incidents 1–15

Green pipelines, artifact mismatches, parallel pipeline collisions, runner failures, cache problems, identity federation, infrastructure retries, shared templates, build dependencies, registry throttling, and emergency hotfix failures.

Category 2 — Git, GitOps & Release Management | Incidents 16–25

GitOps reconciliation failures, emergency hotfixes, stale configuration, release-branch divergence, mutable release references, shared configuration blast radius, and automation ownership conflicts.

Category 3 — IaC & Infrastructure Automation | Incidents 26–37

Terraform destructive replacements, state split-brain, provider upgrades, shared module regressions, infrastructure drift, partial applies, bootstrap dependency loops, state-lock incidents, dependency races, irreversible infrastructure changes, and cross-environment blast radius.

Category 4 — Containers, Kubernetes & Deployment Mechanics | Incidents 38–50

Image digest mismatches, registry replication lag, image-pull storms, multi-architecture failures, admission webhooks, mutating webhook timeouts, stale configuration, rollout deadlocks, scheduling changes, storage attachment failures, DaemonSet capacity problems, Kubernetes API overload, and GitOps controller failures.

What you will learn from each incident

Every production incident follows a practical investigation structure:

Symptoms → Investigation → Root Cause → Immediate Fix → Long-Term Prevention

2 interview follow-ups + 1 curveball + a production Pro Tip

The goal is not memorizing answers.

The goal is learning how a modern DevOps engineer thinks during a production failure.

Professor Brian Greene the physicist reveals the biggest questions about Artificial Intelligence physics, string theory, Simulation theory, god, religion, christianity and more

Professor Brian Greene is a theoretical physicist, mathematician, and Professor of Physics and Mathematics at Columbia University, where he also directs the Center for Theoretical Physics. He is a leading researcher in string theory, the co-founder of the World Science Festival, and the bestselling author of several books, including ‘Until the End of Time: Mind, Matter, and Our Search for Meaning in an Evolving Universe’.

records.description:
Meditators like Annaka Harris have long examined the mind from the inside. They've arrived at some shocking ideas: that the self and free will may both be illusions. Science is only now catching up. | Subscribe to Futurology! https://linkin.bio/futurology

Science studies the world from the outside. But for thousands of years, meditators have been running a different experiment: sit still, pay close attention, and watch what reality does. The results of those experiments can feel unintuitive. The self is an illusion. Free will too. There is no thing that exists without other things. Here's the strange part: at the frontiers of physics, the science is catching up to this ancient wisdom.

In this episode, author Annaka Harris tells the story of a lifetime spent watching her own mind, from the childhood migraines that taught her to meditate to the formation of the question she now asks leading physicists and philosophers. What if it's awareness all the way down? Her forthcoming book is Unlocking Consciousness: How Solving the Mystery Could Provoke a Scientific Revolution. That revolution begins with a wager: that felt experience is not something the brain produces but what the universe is made of.

records.description:
A Conversation with Cameron Berg (Ep. 487)

Sam Harris speaks with Cameron Berg about whether AI systems are or could become conscious. They discuss self-reports in LLMs, what models say when deception is switched off, the "bliss attractor" state, consciousness and sentience, the hard problem of consciousness, parallels between neural networks and biological brains, the moral risk of building minds that can suffer, possible parallels to factory farming, moral patienthood, the alignment problem, and other topics.  

Cameron Berg is the founder and director of Reciprocal Research, a nonprofit AI research lab. Using mechanistic interpretability, computational neuroscience, and psychometric tools, he studies whether frontier AI systems exhibit computational properties associated with consciousness. His aim is to reduce uncertainty about the kinds of cognitive systems we are building, an important but neglected component of the alignment problem. A cognitive science graduate of Yale and former Meta AI resident, he writes regularly about these questions in The Wall Street Journal, and his research has been covered by The Washington Post. He is the subject of the feature documentary AM I?.

Website: https://reciprocalresearch.org/

If you’ve tried meditation and felt like nothing changed, this explains why and what an effective “dose” really looks like.

What Actually Happens to Your Brain When You Meditate

Sit still. Focus on your breath. Notice when your mind wanders, and gently bring it back. It sounds almost too simple to do anything measurable — and yet a genuinely large body of neuroscience research has spent the past two decades documenting exactly what this practice does to the physical brain.

In this video, we break down what's actually been measured: consistent changes in amygdala reactivity and prefrontal regulation after structured training, the more complex (and harder to prove causally) findings from long-term practitioner studies, and what the research says actually matters for getting real benefit — consistency over weeks, not intensity of any single session.

If this changed how you'll approach starting a meditation practice, subscribe — we're covering how to actually build a consistent daily habit next.

records.description:
What really happens inside your brain when you meditate? 🧠🧘

In a world of constant notifications, deadlines, social media and information overload, our minds are rarely truly quiet.

But meditation may offer something surprisingly powerful—not an escape from modern life, but a way to change how we respond to it.

In this 25-minute documentary, we explore the fascinating connection between ancient meditation practices and modern neuroscience.

From dhyana and breath awareness to brain imaging and modern psychological research, discover what science currently tells us about meditation, attention, stress and emotional regulation.

🔬 In this documentary, you'll discover:

🧠 What happens in the brain during meditation
😌 How meditation may influence stress and emotional responses
🌬️ The science behind mindful breathing
🎯 How meditation trains attention and awareness
🏛️ The connection between ancient Indian contemplative traditions and modern neuroscience
🧬 What scientists mean by neuroplasticity
🧠 What research says about the amygdala, prefrontal cortex and hippocampus
🔬 What brain-imaging studies can—and cannot—tell us
❤️ How mindfulness may support mental well-being
🌙 The potential relationship between meditation, sleep and emotional balance
⚡ Why consistency may matter more than long meditation sessions

🕉️ Ancient Wisdom. Modern Science.

For thousands of years, contemplative traditions have explored attention, awareness and the nature of the mind.

Today, neuroscience is investigating some of the same questions using MRI, brain imaging, behavioral experiments and clinical research.

But science also teaches us to be careful.

Meditation is not a magical cure and claims about “rewiring the brain” should not be exaggerated. The evidence is promising, but researchers are still studying exactly how meditation affects brain function, brain structure and mental health.

This documentary separates scientific evidence from popular claims and explores what we actually know.

🧘 Try this with us

Take a few minutes.

Sit comfortably.

Breathe naturally.

Notice your thoughts.

Don't fight them.

Simply observe.

STOP. BREATHE. OBSERVE.

And discover what happens when you give your mind a moment of silence.

⚠️ Important Disclaimer

This video is for educational and informational purposes only. Meditation may support well-being, but it should not be considered a replacement for professional medical or mental-health care. If you are experiencing significant psychological distress, consult a qualified healthcare professional.

records.description:
In this episode, Niall speaks with Liam McClintock, a Yale graduate, former Buddhist monk, and founder of FitMind, a meditation training platform that helps people move beyond stress reduction into deeper states of awareness and well-being.

After leaving a career in finance, Liam spent three years training in monasteries across Asia, studying under Bhante Vimalaramsi and learning advanced meditation practices, including jhana states and forgiveness meditation. He recently published his first book, “FitMind”, which brings together neuroscience and contemplative practice in practical tools for everyday life.

In this conversation, they explore:

— Why happiness supports meditation, not the other way around

— How predictive processing theory helps explain why meditation reduces suffering

— The neuroscience of jhana states and their role in reshaping the mind

— A forgiveness practice for letting go of emotional baggage

— The four-step framework for training attention: recognize, release, relish, and remain

You can learn more about Liam's work at https://fitmind.org.

---

Liam is the founder of FitMind, a mental fitness training platform that provides evidence-based programmes for individuals and organisations, including Uber. After studying history at Yale University and briefly working in finance, he left his career in 2018 to become a certified yoga and meditation teacher in Bali. His interest in the mind grew from a childhood diagnosis of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), leading him to explore psychology, lucid dreaming, and a wide range of contemplative traditions. His training has included Theravada Buddhism in India, Sri Lanka, and Malaysia; Indigenous shamanism in Peru and Mexico; Boabom, an ancient Tibetan martial art, in Chile; Hatha and Ashtanga Yoga in Indonesia and Nepal; Tibetan Buddhist practices in Bhutan; and Dzogchen, Mahamudra, Qi Gong, and other contemplative disciplines in the United States. Liam later completed a Master of Science in Applied Neuroscience at King's College London, where his dissertation examined the neural correlates of advanced nondual meditation.

Liam has since become a Buddhist monk to deepen his meditation practice and has participated in consciousness research at Harvard University. He has also advised on advanced meditation training for Harvard Medical School and Massachusetts General Hospital. Drawing on both scientific research and first-hand contemplative experience, Liam's work bridges neuroscience and ancient wisdom traditions to help people cultivate greater mental fitness, resilience, and wellbeing. He believes that making mental fitness an accessible and enjoyable part of everyday life has the potential to improve both individual lives and society as a whole.

records.description:
What if our ancient ancestors experienced the world through sound as much as sight? In this episode I'm joined by Greg Moffitt — writer, broadcaster and host of the long-running Legalise Freedom podcast — to talk about archaeoacoustics: the study of how ancient sites were built to sound, not just to look.

https://legalise-freedom.com/

We get into why stone circles like Stonehenge and Avebury may have been deliberately shaped to reflect and focus sound, the "stone tape theory" and its roots in 1970s British TV, why cathedrals function almost like instruments, and the bicameral mind theory of consciousness. From there we go further out — sound as a weapon, the pyramids as a possible power source, and a run through the competing theories on where (and whether) Atlantis actually existed, including catastrophism and the idea that human history may include a forgotten global reset.

Greg has spent over a decade interviewing researchers on the edges of mainstream thought through Legalise Freedom, and this conversation ranges from hard acoustics to speculative history — with the ground rules made clear as we go.

Conservatives have been telling us to wake up decades before anyone had heard of being woke.

Chapters and AI summary:

Shawn Whatley interviews Danny Randall, a doctoral student in intellectual history at the University of Buckingham and managing director of Foundations Forum, about his claim that “Western civilization is already dead,” arguing that the inherited norms and mores many associate with the West—often remembered as strong in the 1990s—no longer exist in the same form amid rapid cultural change, crime, altered education, and declining affordability. Randall outlines his PhD research on the shift from religious toleration to secular pluralism in Britain and Canada, discusses how axiomatic ideas can drive secularization, and explores breaks from tradition since the 1960s, including the sexual revolution and family breakdown. They debate liberalism, John Stuart Mill, neutrality and the state, factionalism, and civic education, and conclude with Randall’s call for communal “public houses” and his Foundations Forum newsletter and events aimed at recovering Western intellectual, spiritual, and cultural heritage.

records.description:
Can you actually hear the invisible signal from a TV remote? 🤯📺🔊

In this experiment, I found a simple way to turn the invisible signal from a remote control into something you can actually hear through a speaker!

I connected an IR receiver to an audio amplifier and pointed different remote controls at the sensor. When the remote sends its infrared signal, the receiver detects the rapid pulses and the speaker turns them into an audible sound.

It's a surprisingly simple experiment that lets you hear what a remote control normally does invisibly!

🔧 In this experiment:
• IR / Infrared Receiver
• TV Remote Control
• Audio Amplifier
• Speaker
• Infrared Signal
• Remote Control Pulses

You'll also see what happens when the remote is pointed directly at the IR receiver and how the sound changes when the signal is detected.

0:00 – Session Intro

1:05 – Energy as a Shifting Sphere
Experiences himself as a morphing, plastic energy unit in Focus 15.

2:17 – Narrowing Into a Beam
Sphere compresses into a directed column of energy.

2:37 – Entering Focus 21
White and yellow colors intermingle; expanded state reached.

3:01 – Becoming Light
Experiencing light from the inside rather than observing it.

3:41 – Branching Like Roots
Energy spreads downward; dark areas with green dots appear.

4:41 – A Familiar Face
Glimpses Karen, senses Alexander; light source grows above.

5:34 – Air Moving Through the Body
Energy flows directly through Jeremy's physical form.

5:47 – An Older Man's Face
Shadowy face with a pronounced chin appears, then fades.

7:18 – Physical Awareness Returns
Hand feels disembodied; tape on fingers noticed from a distance.

7:55 – Pressure on the Forehead
Strong third-eye pressure builds; Jeremy bends backward.

8:57 – The Yellow Saturn Disc
A glowing yellow disc forms around his head at the pressure point.

10:16 – A Female Figure Appears
Translucent blue female form emerges; a deep male voice stirs.

11:29 – First Contact: "Hello"
The entity speaks its first word; facilitator encourages a response.

12:18 – Entity Enjoys the Blend
The voice settles in; works to convince Jeremy this is real.

13:56 – Skeptical Yet Curious
Entity reads Jeremy's duality — doubting and open at the same time.

14:54 – "Split"
Entity describes Jeremy as opened in halves; plays with the word "unhinged."

16:16 – "Jeremy Is Us"
Entity reveals itself as a group consciousness with no true separation from Jeremy.

18:50 – The Blue Light in the Photos
Three photos with undefined blue light identified as their energy pattern.

19:42 – Searching for the Right Word
"Tentacles," "spines," "extensions" — none quite capture their infinite reach.

20:51 – Infinite Energy
They are infinite energy portions with infinite capabilities.

21:54 – Fiber Optics of Consciousness
They focus energy to specific areas, like fiber optics, for innumerable reasons.

25:12 – Can You Help Us?
Asked about freedom; entity says true freedom is found within.

26:24 – Sub-Extensions & Group Souls
Separate humans can be extensions of the same group consciousness.

29:23 – Earth as Compressed Learning
Earth is one of only three points where advancement can be dramatically accelerated.

30:24 – Don't Preconceive Your Source
Key message: don't assume where your guidance is coming from.

Facilitator asks; entity agrees to offer two syllables.

31:36 – The Name "Ourma"
An energy shape as much as a sound; meaning embedded in the letters themselves.

Different voices, same unified source and information.

34:25 – Time Is Your Creation
Time was designed to allow compressed, intensive experience and rapid growth.

37:08 – Three Special Points in the Universe
Earth and two others form an energy triangle; locations cannot be measured by distance.

38:42 – Entity Withdraws
Notes Jeremy's natural ability and gracefully exits.

40:42 – Jeremy Slowly Returns
Still partly in his energy body; guided back through focus levels.

42:57 – Counting Down
Counted from 10 to 1; full return in perfect health and balance.

43:43 – Full Body Buzz
Every cell buzzing with energy; barely sure he can walk.

44:19 – Never Done This Before
Reflects on a failed attempt at automatic writing; this was entirely new.

46:00 – "He's Got a Deep Voice"
Jeremy recalls the contact clearly; it got easier the longer it flowed.

46:19 – An Octave Below Normal
Vocal cords felt extended; speaking far below his natural singing range.

First session documented; people begin arriving and the tape is shut off.

records.description:
Binaural beats are often grouped with frequency music and sound therapy, but they work in a very different way.

A binaural beat is not a tone physically played into the room. It arises from the difference between two tones presented separately to the left and right ear.

If the left ear receives 200 Hz and the right ear 210 Hz, the difference is 10 Hz. No loudspeaker is producing a 10 Hz tone. Instead, the auditory system perceives a rhythmic difference while processing both signals.

The binaural beat therefore exists primarily in perception.

This is important within the philosophy of *ChannelWaves® – Sound in Motion*. Sound can be heard, but it also moves physically through air, matter and the body. Music contains complex relationships between frequencies, harmonics, dynamics and spatial movement.

Binaural beats are different. They depend specifically on presenting slightly different information to each ear.

Why Headphones Are Essential?

True binaural beats require stereo headphones.

The left and right ears must receive different frequencies independently. If 200 Hz is sent to the left ear and 210 Hz to the right, those signals must remain separated until they enter the auditory system.

With loudspeakers, both ears hear both speakers. The tones mix in the room before reaching the listener. Headphones are therefore not simply convenient; they are part of the technique itself.

This is almost the opposite of the ChannelWaves® approach. Within ChannelWaves®, loudspeakers are used deliberately so music can exist as a physical sound field around the listener. Harmonics, dynamics, spatial movement and the full frequency spectrum become part of the experience.

Binaural beats rely on separation of the ears rather than immersion of the whole body in one acoustic space.

Why Keep Binaural Beats Pure?

Many binaural recordings are combined with relaxing music, synthesizers or nature sounds. That may make them more pleasant to hear, but it also makes the signal more complex.

Music is never just a background carrier. Music itself is information.

A composition contains rhythm, melody, harmonics, dynamics, phrasing and constantly changing frequency relationships. Once music is added, two different systems are working at the same time.

If someone relaxes while listening to music containing a 6 Hz binaural beat, what caused the response? The binaural difference, the tempo, the harmony, the dynamics, the emotional response to the music, or the combination?

For that reason, I prefer to keep the two separate.

If we want to use binaural beats as a specific auditory principle, they should be presented as cleanly as possible: two stable tones, one for each ear, with one controlled difference between them.

And if we use music, we should allow music itself to do the work.

Within ChannelWaves®, the composition is the frequency architecture. Rhythm, harmonics, intervals, dynamics and movement form one integrated design. A binaural beat is a separate technique with a different mechanism.

From Delta to Gamma

Binaural beats are usually described by the difference between the two carrier tones:

Delta – approximately 0.5 to 4 Hz.** Associated mainly with deep sleep and deep rest.

Theta – approximately 4 to 8 Hz.** Often associated with drowsiness, inward attention and deep relaxation.

Alpha – approximately 8 to 13 Hz.** Associated with relaxed wakefulness and calm attention.

Beta – approximately 13 to 30 Hz.** Commonly associated with active thinking, concentration and task-oriented activity.

Gamma – approximately 30 Hz and above.** Associated with complex processing and integration.

These ranges should not be seen as switches. A 6 Hz difference does not simply place the brain into Theta, and a 40 Hz difference does not automatically create a Gamma state.

The Brain Is Not a Frequency Selector!

One of the biggest misunderstandings surrounding binaural beats is the idea that the brain behaves like a radio.

Choose 6 Hz: Theta.
Choose 10 Hz: Alpha.
Choose 40 Hz: Gamma.

The human system is far more complex.

Brain activity never consists of one single frequency. Different regions can show different patterns at the same time, while breathing, attention, emotion, memory and sensory input continue to interact.

A binaural beat is therefore better understood as an auditory stimulus, not as a command to the brain.

And perhaps that is what makes it so interesting.

Two frequencies enter the ears. A third rhythmic experience appears to arise from their relationship. That third frequency is not simply played to us.

Part of the experience is created by our own system.

Binaural beats therefore remind us of something fundamental about sound: what we experience is determined not only by the frequencies outside the body, but also by what our own system does with them.

More info: www.ChannelWay.nl
